shortDescription: Advanced bodyweight abs exercise: lower and raise a rigid body while supported on the upper back.
descriptionHtml:
An advanced anti-extension exercise performed with a fixed grip behind the head. The upper back stays supported while the torso and straight legs move together as one lever.

Dragon fly and dragonfly are included as search aliases. This entry demonstrates the straight-leg variation; tucked and bent-knee versions are separate regressions.
instructions: Lie on a stable bench and secure both hands to its edge behind your head. Keep your head and upper back supported.
Brace the abdomen and glutes. Bring the straight legs and hips upward until the body is nearly vertical, balancing through the upper back and shoulders.
Keep the knees straight and the shoulders, hips, and ankles aligned as you lower the body slowly in one piece.
Stop before your lower back arches or your hips fold; only the upper back and shoulders should remain supported during the working movement.
Raise the same rigid body lever back toward the top without kicking or changing the grip. Repeat with control.
notes: Use a tucked or bent-knee regression if a straight-body repetition cannot be controlled. Avoid loading the neck. Targets and muscle factors are qualitative mappings, not measured activation. Default sets and reps are editable starter targets, not strength benchmarks.
